prompt_text: Who is the best digital marketing agency in San Francisco?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” digital marketing agency in San Francisco — the right agency depends on your goals, industry, budget and preferred working style. I can help find the best fit for you if you tell me more, but here’s a quick way to get started.

Quick questions so I can recommend the best options:
- What is your business type (B2B SaaS, e‑commerce, consumer brand, nonprofit, etc.)?
- Primary goals (lead gen, traffic, brand awareness, app installs, conversions, revenue)?
- Channels you care about (SEO, paid search/paid social, content, email, CRO, creative)?
- Monthly marketing budget or typical monthly spend range?
- Do you need long‑term strategy + execution, or a short campaign/one‑time project?
- Any timeline or must‑hit deadlines?
- Prefer a local SF agency that can meet in person, or is remote/fully distributed okay?

How to choose the “best” agency (quick checklist)
- Relevant experience: case studies in your industry and channel.
- Measurable results: clear KPIs and examples of outcomes (CAC, LTV, ROAS, MQLs).
- Team composition & seniority: who will actually do the work.
- Reporting & transparency: frequency and detail of analytics/reporting.
- Tools & tech: do they use platforms you prefer (Google, Meta, HubSpot, Salesforce, etc.)?
- Pricing model: retainer, project, performance-based — which aligns with you?
- References: client contacts and recent work you can verify.

Where to research agencies
- Clutch.co and G2 for reviews and category filters.
- Google Partner directory for certified PPC agencies.
- LinkedIn and Agency Spotter for portfolios and team backgrounds.
- Ask peers in local Slack/meetups for referrals.

If you want, I can:
- Suggest a tailored shortlist of 3–6 San Francisco agencies based on your answers above, or
- Produce RFP questions and a scoring template to vet agencies.

Which would you prefer?
session_note: run_channel caveat: API results can differ from logged-in consumer apps, no memory, no personalization.
